items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo’s Al-Nassr faces unwanted injury woes after AFC Champions League win vs Al-Sadd as Kingsley Coman’s recovery timeline emerges
items.description:
The French winger's latest appearance ended far sooner than expected, raising fresh concerns about his fitness as the Saudi side continues its pursuit of domestic and continental success. 
Cristiano Ronaldo and Al-Nassr secured another important AFC Champions League Elite victory against Al-Sadd, but the celebrations at Al-Awwal Park were overshadowed by an early setback involving Kingsley Coman. The French winger’s latest appearance ended far sooner than expected, raising fresh concerns about his fitness as the Saudi side continues its pursuit of domestic and continental success.



Al-Nassr eventually claimed a 2-1 victory on Tuesday, thanks to Ronaldo’s penalty and a spectacular overhead kick from Joao Felix. However, Coman’s departure after only a few minutes left Ange Postecoglou with another potential injury problem to manage. Ronaldo opened the scoring from the penalty spot in the 13th minute after being fouled inside the area by Mohamed Camara. 



The Portuguese forward calmly converted to register his 987th career goal, moving within 13 strikes of the historic 1,000-goal milestone. Al-Sadd responded through Mohammed Waad, who finished Akram Afif’s clever attacking move in the 22nd minute. However, the goalscorer went from hero to villain shortly before half-time, receiving a straight red card after a VAR review found that he had spat at Al-Nassr defender Nawaf Boushal. 



Despite playing against 10 men, Ange Postecoglou’s players struggled to completely dominate the visitors. Joao Felix eventually provided the decisive moment in the 52nd minute, producing a stunning bicycle kick from the edge of the penalty area that left goalkeeper Meshaal Barsham with no chance.



PLUS QUE 13 BUTS AVANT LES 1000 🔥🐐Cristiano Ronaldo 🇵🇹 a inscrit son 987e en carrière et permet à Al Nassr de prendre les devants face à Al Sadd 🇶🇦 en AFC Ligue des Champions Élite ! pic.twitter.com/JIQ9XKvmuY— SPL 🇸🇦 (@ActuSPL) November 24, 2026 



The victory moved Al-Nassr to nine points and fifth place in the AFC Champions League Elite West Region standings, with a postponed fixture against Al-Wasl still to come. Al-Sadd remained 14th with only two points from five matches.



Coman suffers another frustrating setback



The biggest concern for Postecoglou came almost immediately after kick-off, when Coman went down following an early sprint and challenge. The French winger was unable to continue and was replaced by Abdullah Al-Hamdan after just three minutes.



The timing was particularly frustrating because the Frenchman was making his first start since returning from a previous injury. The 30-year-old had only recently rejoined the squad, coming off the bench against Al-Ahli before being handed an opportunity from the beginning against Al-Sadd.



Coman substituído com apenas 5 minutos de jogo. pic.twitter.com/BwxGNH41TT— Central do Arabão (@centraldoarabao) November 24, 2026 



His latest setback raises further questions about his physical condition and ability to maintain consistency. Coman has made only nine appearances for Al-Nassr this season, scoring once without registering an assist.



Recovery timeline emerges amid hamstring injury concerns



According to an update shared by Saudi physiotherapist Thamer Al-Shahrani, Coman may have suffered a hamstring injury during a sprint. The assessment remains preliminary, with the exact severity still needing to be established through medical examinations. Al-Shahrani explained on X (formerly Twitter): “Coman has a hamstring injury from the sprint. If it’s a muscle tear, the likely recovery times are: Best case: 10-14 days. Worst case: 4-6 weeks.”



That would leave Al-Nassr facing two very different possibilities depending on the results of further assessments. A minor injury could sideline Coman for around two weeks, while a more serious muscle tear could keep him out for up to six weeks.



Kingsley Coman of team Al Nassr is tackled by Paulo Otavio of team Al Sadd SC 



The winger’s previous injury makes the situation particularly concerning. He suffered a hamstring problem during Al-Nassr’s 3-1 Champions League Elite victory over Neftchi Fergana in October, which forced him to miss several Saudi Pro League fixtures and another continental match.



Coman’s recurring fitness problems are becoming an unwanted complication for Postecoglou, who needs his attacking options available as Al-Nassr competes on multiple fronts. The Frenchman arrived with considerable expectations, but his limited availability has made it difficult for him to establish consistent momentum alongside Ronaldo, Felix and Sadio Mane.

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo’s retirement plans after Al-Nassr contract expires take fresh twist as mother Dolores Aveiro breaks silence
items.description:
With the Portuguese superstar approaching another important crossroads at 41, fresh comments from his family have added an unexpected twist to the uncertainty surrounding the final years of his playing career. 
Cristiano Ronaldo’s future beyond his current Al-Nassr contract has become a major talking point following his retirement from international soccer. With the Portuguese superstar approaching another important crossroads at 41, fresh comments from his family have added an unexpected twist to the uncertainty surrounding the final years of his playing career.



Ronaldo remains focused on club soccer and continues to chase the remarkable milestone of 1,000 career goals. However, speculation has grown over whether the ongoing campaign will be his last in Saudi Arabia, particularly with his current agreement approaching its expiration date.



The five-time Ballon d’Or winner signed a two-year contract extension in June 2025, keeping him at Al-Nassr until the end of the 2026-27 season in June 2027. Although reports have suggested that the Saudi club would like to keep its captain for another campaign, no new agreement has been confirmed.



Ronaldo has continued producing impressive numbers, reaching 987 career goals this Tuesday. He has also scored nine times in 11 appearances across the Saudi Pro League and AFC Champions League Elite this season, maintaining his pursuit of the historic 1,000-goal mark.



Cristiano Ronaldo of Al Nassr.



His international retirement on November 5, 2026, has added another dimension to the situation. After 23 years with Portugal, he ended his international career with 234 appearances and 146 goals, allowing him to concentrate entirely on his commitments at club level.



Reports raise questions over the end of his playing career



Speculation intensified after reports suggested Ronaldo could leave Al-Nassr when his contract expires. Portuguese journalist Pedro Sepulveda previously indicated that the current campaign might represent the end of the forward’s time in Saudi Arabia. “I firmly believe that this season could be Cristiano Ronaldo’s last at Al-Nassr,” Sepulveda said, via talkSPORT.



There have also been suggestions that Al-Nassr could organize a major farewell if Ronaldo decides to leave. A possible final appearance against Al-Hilal on May 28, 2027, has been discussed, although neither his departure nor a retirement ceremony has been confirmed.



Ange Postecoglou team Manager of Al Nassr and Cristiano Ronaldo



What did Dolores Aveiro say about retirement speculation?



Ronaldo’s mother, Dolores Aveiro, has now challenged the suggestion that her son intends to retire immediately after his Al-Nassr contract expires. In comments reported by 365Scores Arabic, she directly dismissed the possibility. “It’s not true that Cristiano Ronaldo is thinking of retiring from football after his current contract with Al-Nassr expires,” Aveiro stated.



Her intervention provides a different perspective on the veteran’s plans, particularly as speculation continues over whether he will extend his stay in Riyadh. While her comments do not confirm that Ronaldo will sign another contract, they suggest that ending his playing career in June 2027 should not be treated as a foregone conclusion.



Cristiano Ronaldo of Real Madrid looks on with his mother Maria Dolores dos Santos Aveiro



Ronaldo’s decision could have consequences for Al-Nassr beyond his own career, particularly regarding the future of compatriot Joao Felix. The former Chelsea forward’s contract also runs until June 2027, and journalist Pedro Sepulveda believes his chances of remaining in Saudi Arabia could be closely connected to Ronaldo’s situation.



For now, Ronaldo has time to decide whether he wants to extend his Al-Nassr career, consider another challenge, or eventually retire. The possibility of playing alongside his son, Cristiano Jr., at senior level has also been mentioned as a potential factor in his thinking.

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo sets new Al Nassr milestone with record-breaking goal vs Al Sadd
items.description:
Cristiano Ronaldo broke Abderrazak Hamdallah's record as Al Nassr's top scorer in continental competitions and moved closer to the historic mark of 1,000 career goals. 
Cristiano Ronaldo has added another record to his career by becoming Al Nassr’s all-time top scorer in continental competitions. The Portuguese forward reached the mark with his penalty against Al Sadd in the AFC Champions League Elite, a goal that also gave him his 987th in his professional career.



With the strike from the spot in the 13th minute at Al Awwal Park, Ronaldo reached 16 goals in the AFC Champions League Elite, putting him level with Abderrazak Hamdallah, the former Al Nassr forward who had held the club record. The tally by itself would have only tied the Moroccan, so the figure alone did not settle the question.



What puts Ronaldo clear at the top is a goal he scored in the AFC Champions League Two, the secondary Asian competition. It came in the quarterfinals on April 19, 2026, when he opened the scoring for Al Nassr in a 4-0 win over Al Wasl in Dubai, the 969th goal of his career at that point.



Adding it to his Elite total brings him to 17 in continental competitions, one more than Hamdallah, which makes him the club’s outright leading scorer in that category.



Cristiano Ronaldo 9️⃣8️⃣7️⃣🇵🇹🎥 @Rtiban1 pic.twitter.com/aYo1Ewvouv— Fabrizio Romano (@FabrizioRomano) November 24, 2026 



The record arrived on a night in which the captain had a point to prove, after missing a penalty in the loss to Al Ahli last Friday, a match in which he had also scored. His conversion against Al Sadd ended his run of missed penalties and gave him another landmark in a season in which he continues to chase more titles with Al Nassr in Saudi Arabia.



Where does Ronaldo stand in the race to 1,000 goals?


        


With the penalty against Al Sadd, Ronaldo moved to 987 career goals, leaving him 13 away from the historic mark of 1,000, a milestone that no player has officially reached in competitive matches.



The 41-year-old has kept up a steady pace this season, with 11 goals in 14 matches across all competitions, including a hat trick against Al Kholood on October 29 and his goal against Al Ahli last Friday.



The chase now depends almost entirely on his club form, as both he and Lionel Messi have stepped away from international duty with their national teams. Messi, for his part, is at 937 career goals, which leaves Ronaldo comfortably ahead in the race for a historic mark in soccer.

items.title: Real Madrid vs PSV: Confirmed lineups for the 2026-27 UEFA Champions League match
items.description:
Take a look at the projected lineups for Real Madrid vs PSV in the 2026-27 UEFA Champions League. Real Madrid host PSV at a point in the season where both sides are trying to settle into a rhythm in the Champions League, and this one pits a Madrid side on a run of wins against a PSV team still looking for consistency on the road.
Real Madrid come into this one on a three-game winning streak, having beaten AEK Athens 3-2 on November 4, Leipzig 4-1 on October 21 and Roma 4-3 on October 14. Those results have come with goals at both ends, but the outcomes have kept the points at home each time. A win here would make it four straight and tighten their grip on the top of the group picture.
PSV arrive off a mixed stretch, losing 1-2 to Brugge on November 4 after beating Porto 1-0 on October 20, and that followed a 0-1 loss to Leipzig on October 13. The Dutch side have shown they can get results against sides in and around their level, but the defeats to Brugge and Leipzig point to problems against tougher opposition. Three points in Madrid would be a major statement for Peter Bosz’s team and a real boost to their path through the group.
Real Madrid confirmed lineup
Mourinho sets Real Madrid up in a 4-2-3-1 with Courtois behind a back four of Valverde, Militão, Rüdiger and Cucurella. Tchouaméni and Camavinga sit as the double pivot, giving the side control in midfield, while Brahim Díaz and Yan Diomande support Mbappé and Vinícius Júnior further forward. With no absences listed, Mourinho has his first-choice attacking options available, and the front four carries real pace and directness in behind a PSV back line that will have to defend a lot of space.
Real Madrid confirmed starting XI (4-3-3): Thibaut Courtois, Federico Valverde, Marc Cucurella, Aurélien Tchouaméni, Éder Militão, Antonio Rüdiger, Bernardo Silva, Arda Güler, Kylian Mbappé, Yan Diomande, Vinícius Júnior. Coach: Jose Mourinho.
PSV confirmed lineup
Bosz lines PSV up in a matching 4-2-3-1, with Kovář in goal behind Dest, Geertruida, Obispo and Kostić. Sano and Mijnans anchor the midfield, with Fernández, Perišić and Til playing behind lone striker Ruben van Bommel. There are no absences to work around, so Bosz can pick his preferred XI, but the away side will need their midfield pair to hold firm against Madrid’s movement through the middle if they are to keep the game close.
PSV confirmed starting XI (4-2-3-1): Matěj Kovář, Sergiño Dest, Filip Kostić, Kodai Sano, Lutsharel Geertruida, Armando Obispo, Ivan Perišić, Paul Wanner, Guus Til, Sven Mijnans, Ruben van Bommel. Coach: Peter Bosz.

items.title: Arsenal vs Dortmund: Confirmed lineups for the 2026-27 UEFA Champions League match
items.description:
Take a look at the projected lineups for Arsenal vs Dortmund in the 2026-27 UEFA Champions League. Arsenal host Dortmund at the Emirates in a Champions League meeting between two sides who have found different ways to stay competitive this season.
Arsenal come into this on the back of a 2-1 win over Slavia Praha on November 4, a 2-2 draw with Bayern on October 21 and a 3-0 win over Lille on October 13. That run shows a team capable of grinding out results against tough opponents while still scoring freely when the matchup favors them. A strong showing here would keep Arsenal firmly in the mix at the top of the league phase table.
Dortmund arrive having beaten Betis 2-1 on November 4, a follow-up to a 2-1 win over Sabah FK on October 20, though they did lose 0-1 to Bodo Glimt back on October 14. The two wins either side of that defeat suggest Dortmund have settled into a rhythm after a rocky patch. Three points in London would be a significant statement for a side looking to prove they belong among the competition’s top sides.
Arsenal confirmed lineup
Arteta sets Arsenal up in a 4-2-3-1 with Kepa in goal behind a back line of Ben White, Ezri Konsa, Gabriel Magalhães and Piero Hincapié. Declan Rice and Martín Odegaard anchor the midfield, with Odegaard pushed into a more advanced creative role alongside Myles Lewis-Skelly and Noni Madueke supporting Viktor Gyökeres up top. Christos Tzolis rounds out the attacking line, giving Arsenal width and pace to work off Gyökeres as the central reference point.
Arsenal confirmed starting XI (4-2-3-1): Kepa Arrizabalaga, Ben White, Piero Hincapié, Declan Rice, Ezri Konsa, Gabriel Magalhães, Noni Madueke, Myles Lewis-Skelly, Viktor Gyökeres, Martin Ødegaard, Christos Tzolis. Coach: Mikel Arteta.
Dortmund confirmed lineup
Kovač goes with a 3-4-2-1 shape for Dortmund, with Gregor Kobel behind a back three of Kouakou Joane Gadou, Nico Schlotterbeck and Waldemar Anton. Konstantinos Karetsas and Julian Ryerson provide the width as wing-backs, while Felix Nmecha and Jobe Bellingham control the center of the park. Maximilian Beier and Daniel Svensson sit just behind Fábio Silva, giving Dortmund two players to link midfield and attack around a lone central striker.
Dortmund confirmed starting XI (3-4-2-1): Gregor Kobel, Julian Ryerson, Daniel Svensson, Nico Schlotterbeck, Waldemar Anton, Joane Gadou, Felix Nmecha, Joey Veerman, Fábio Silva, Jobe Bellingham, Maximilian Beier. Coach: Niko Kovač.

items.title: Why is Jude Bellingham not starting for Real Madrid vs PSV in the 2026-27 Champions League?
items.description:
Jude Bellingham begins Real Madrid's Champions League match against PSV on the bench, in a decision that reportedly responds to his heavy workload this season. 
Jude Bellingham is not part of Real Madrid’s starting lineup for the Champions League clash against PSV Eindhoven at the Santiago Bernabeu, a surprise on matchday five of the league phase. The England midfielder begins the match on the bench, in a decision that appears to come from Jose Mourinho himself.



The move seems to be purely sporting. Mourinho is reportedly giving Bellingham a rest to manage his workload, and the player is neither injured nor suspended. That explanation fits with the numbers, as Bellingham arrives at the PSV match after a heavy workload. 



This season he has appeared in 17 matches for Real Madrid between LaLiga and the Champions League, starting 16 of them, with an average of roughly 82 minutes per game.



In his place, Arda Guler enters the midfield, in a slightly more withdrawn role than Bellingham’s, behind an attack of Vinicius Junior, Yan Diomande and Kylian Mbappe.




📋✅ ¡Nuestro XI inicial!🆚 @PSV pic.twitter.com/XGjFbydvd4— Real Madrid C.F. (@realmadrid) November 24, 2026




Real Madrid arrive with a perfect record in the league phase, having won all four matches for 12 points, which leaves them second behind Paris Saint-Germain only on goal difference. PSV, meanwhile, sit 25th with four points and need a positive result to improve their chances of reaching the knockout stages.



Bellingham reportedly close to renewing with Real Madrid


        


The decision to rest Bellingham comes at a time when his future at the club appears to be close to settled. According to reports from Fabrizio Romano, Real Madrid and the England midfielder have reached a verbal agreement on a new five-year contract that would keep him at the Bernabeu until 2031, with the formalities still being finalized.



His current deal runs until the summer of 2029, so the extension would add two more years to his stay. The deal has not been officially announced by the club, although reports suggest that the announcement could come not long from now.



For now, Bellingham will watch the start of the match against PSV from the bench, but his place in Mourinho’s plans seems far from being in doubt. The rest should help him stay fresh for the busy stretch ahead, while also making him a strong option to reinforce the team whenever Mourinho feels it is necessary.

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo’s mother Dolores Aveiro reveals major update on possible Portugal return after international retirement
items.description:
Ronaldo's mother's latest reported comments offer a clearer indication of where the 41-year-old stands following a difficult end to his 23-year career with the national team. 
Cristiano Ronaldo’s international future has taken another significant turn after his mother, Dolores Aveiro, addressed the possibility of him reversing his decision to retire from Portugal. Her latest reported comments offer a clearer indication of where the veteran stands following a difficult end to his 23-year career with the national team.



The five-time Ballon d’Or winner announced his retirement on November 5, 2026, bringing an end to one of the most successful international careers in soccer history. However, the circumstances surrounding his departure, particularly his disagreement with head coach Jorge Jesus, have continued to generate debate in Portugal.



Ronaldo finished his international career with 234 appearances and 146 goals, both men’s world records. He also collected 141 victories with Portugal and helped the national team win three major trophies: Euro 2016 and the UEFA Nations League in 2019 and 2025.



His journey began in August 2003, when he made his senior debut against Kazakhstan. Although his first major tournament ended in disappointment with the defeat to Greece in the Euro 2004 final, he eventually became the central figure in the country’s transformation into an international trophy winner.



Cristiano Ronaldo celebrates his goal for Portugal



Ronaldo’s final major tournament was the 2026 World Cup, where he scored three goals in five appearances. His final international strike came against Croatia in the Round of 32 on July 2, while his last appearance for the Selecao was a 1-0 Nations League victory over Wales on September 24.



Disagreement with Jorge Jesus contributed to his departure



Ronaldo’s retirement followed a breakdown in relations with Portugal head coach Jorge Jesus. The disagreement reportedly began after the forward was left on the bench against Norway in September, despite believing he had an understanding with the manager that he would receive around 30 minutes of playing time.



After warming up without being introduced, Ronaldo reportedly became frustrated with the situation. He subsequently left Portugal’s training camp in Copenhagen after being informed that he would not start the following fixture against Denmark.



Pedro Proenca, Cristiano Ronaldo, and Jorge Jesus



Although Jesus was reportedly preparing to include the veteran forward in his November plans, Ronaldo announced his retirement before the squad was revealed. In his farewell message, he insisted: “I leave with my head held high, proud of the path I have taken and knowing that I gave everything I had for Portugal.”



Dolores Aveiro reveals Ronaldo’s intention



Dolores Aveiro’s latest comments suggest that the possibility of Ronaldo returning to international soccer is effectively off the table. “Cristiano Ronaldo has made his final decision and isn’t considering reversing his international retirement.”, she said in an interview with 365Scores Arabic.



The reported remarks reinforce the impression that the former Portugal captain has no plans to reconsider his choice, despite the possibility of a future reconciliation with the national team. His attention remains on club soccer with Al-Nassr, where he is continuing his pursuit of 1,000 career goals.



Dolores Aveiro (mãe de CR7): "Claro que o Cristiano Ronaldo ficou triste, enganaram-no e eu também estou triste. Foi uma derrota [contra a Dinamarca] e foi bem feita, fiquei contente."Está aí o vosso capitão. E ainda manda a mãe. Nem é homenzinho para dizer publicamente o que… pic.twitter.com/xo1ifXZH64— O Fura-Redes (@OFuraRedes) November 16, 2026 



Aveiro had already attracted considerable attention with her comments about the circumstances surrounding her son’s departure. Speaking at an event at Sporting CP’s Estadio Jose Alvalade on November 16, she claimed Ronaldo had been “deceived” and disrespected by the national team, adding that she was pleased Portugal had subsequently suffered a 4-1 defeat to Denmark.



She also criticized the tribute paid to Ronaldo before that match, when Portugal’s players wore his No. 7 shirt. “The tribute should have been done in front of him, not without him,” she argued, suggesting that Sporting CP would be a more appropriate place for a proper farewell.

items.title: Copa America returns to USA in 2028: Why the USMNT isn’t qualified yet and how it can earn a spot
items.description:
The Copa America returns to the United States in 2028, but the USMNT must earn its place through the 2027 Gold Cup, with no automatic spot confirmed yet. 
The Copa America is heading back to the United States in 2028, but the host nation will have to earn its place in the field. CONMEBOL and Concacaf announced an extension of their strategic partnership to organize the 49th edition together, scheduled from June 9 to July 9, 2028, after the two confederations teamed up for the 2024 tournament.



The competition will feature 16 national teams, made up of the 10 CONMEBOL members and six Concacaf representatives. Unlike the last edition, which the U.S. also hosted, Concacaf has stated that its six teams will qualify based on sporting merit, which means the USMNT has no automatic berth confirmed and will need to earn its way in like everyone else.



The path runs through the 2027 Concacaf Gold Cup, played between June 17 and July 11, 2027. The USMNT has already secured its place in that tournament through the Nations League, where it won its quarterfinal series.



The Gold Cup will use a new format, with 16 teams split into two groups of eight, each team playing four group matches and the top four from each group advancing to a single-match knockout phase, starting with the quarterfinals. The draw is set for April 8, 2027.




Concacaf President Victor Montagliani announces the extension of our strategic partnership with CONMEBOL to co-organize the 2028 Copa América in the United States.Six Concacaf national teams will earn their place through the 2027 Concacaf Gold Cup.🏆▶️ Watch his message pic.twitter.com/rgDj9LjjW1— Concacaf (@Concacaf) November 24, 2026




What remains unclear is exactly how Gold Cup results will translate into the six Copa America berths. Concacaf said that the qualification mechanisms for its national teams, along with the host cities, venues and match schedule, will be announced in the near future.



For the USMNT, that means a deep run in the Gold Cup is the only confirmed route to a Copa America at home, and one that will test the squad less than a year after the 2026 World Cup.


        


USA chases a sixth Copa America appearance



The United States has taken part in the Copa America five times: in 1993, 1995, 2007, 2016 and 2024. Its best finish is fourth place, reached in 1995 and again in 2016, when it hosted the Centenario edition and lost in the semifinals to Argentina before falling to Colombia in the third-place match.



The U.S. was also host in 2024, but failed to advance beyond the group stage on home soil, a result that will add pressure to its 2028 campaign if it secures qualification.



It remains the only country outside CONMEBOL to have hosted the tournament, which is why the USMNT will want to be on the field when it returns in 2028 for a sixth appearance.

items.title: Lionel Messi gets different treatment from MLS referees, former Inter Miami boss Phil Neville claims
items.description:
Phil Neville, who coached Inter Miami before Lionel Messi arrived, says the referee's decision on the ball incident against Columbus Crew might have been different if another player had been involved. 
Phil Neville has added his voice to the debate around Lionel Messi and the officiating in Inter Miami’s 3-0 defeat to Columbus Crew in Game 1 of the MLS Cup Playoffs. 



The former Inter Miami coach reportedly suggested that the Argentine is judged differently from other players, particularly after the decision not to send him off for an incident just before halftime.



The play came late in the first half, with Miami already down to ten men and trailing 1-0. Columbus forward Gonzalo Tapia had stepped in front of Messi to stop him from taking a quick throw-in, and Messi responded by throwing the ball at his face.



Referee Allen Chapman showed yellow cards to both players, explaining that the force was negligible and did not amount to violent conduct. Against that backdrop, Jose Armando Rodriguez of Deporte Total USA reported that, for Neville, the referee’s decision was not the right one because it involved Messi. “If it’s Ian Smith throwing the ball, he gets sent off. Lionel Messi doesn’t get sent off,” said the Portland coach, referring to one of his own defenders.



Lionel Messi y Gonzalo Tapia recibieron tarjeta amarilla después de esta acción en la banda.(vía @MLS por Apple TV) pic.twitter.com/kvMAjakAUv— ESPN Deportes (@ESPNDeportes) November 22, 2026 



He also reportedly said that referees have approached certain situations differently since Messi’s arrival to the USA. “Since Messi arrived in MLS, there are situations that referees have handled with common sense,” added the current Portland Timbers coach.



Neville’s words carry extra weight because of his history with the club. He was Inter Miami’s last coach before Messi joined, having been dismissed in June 2023, just before the arrival of the player who would transform the franchise.


        


Inter Miami face a complicated outlook heading into Game 2



The picture is difficult for the defending champions, who now trail 1-0 in a best-of-three series after the heavy loss at Nu Stadium. Game 2 is scheduled for Friday, November 27, at 8 p.m. ET in Columbus, where Inter Miami must avoid defeat to stay alive. A loss would end their title defense in the First Round, while Columbus only need one more win to advance.



If Miami manage to win in Columbus, the series would be level and head to a decisive Game 3 back at Nu Stadium on December 2. In Round One there is no extra time, so if Game 2 is level after 90 minutes, the winner will be decided by a penalty shootout.



The winner of the series would then move on to the Conference Semifinals, set for December 5-6, against the winner of the New England Revolution vs Philadelphia Union series.

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo and Al-Nassr’s key obstacle to defend Saudi Pro League title traced back to one major source in explosive verdict
items.description:
Despite remaining among the leading sides in the Saudi Pro League, frustration is building around the decisions shaping the club’s direction, with supporters increasingly questioning who should be held accountable. 
Cristiano Ronaldo’s future at Al-Nassr has come under renewed scrutiny as the Saudi club faces growing financial pressure and questions over its ability to compete for major honors. Despite remaining among the leading sides in the Saudi Pro League, frustration is building around the decisions shaping the club’s direction, with supporters increasingly questioning who should be held accountable.



The debate has intensified following Al-Nassr’s recent defeat to Al-Ahli, which exposed concerns about squad depth, recruitment and the club’s wider ambitions. While Ronaldo’s enormous wages and performances have also attracted criticism, one particular argument has shifted attention towards the people making the biggest decisions behind the scenes.



Al-Nassr has reportedly accumulated liabilities exceeding 800 million Saudi Riyals, equivalent to around $212-$213 million, following years of expensive recruitment and substantial player contracts. The financial pressure has prompted tighter oversight and restrictions on transfer activity, leaving manager Ange Postecoglou with limited opportunities to strengthen his squad.



The situation has become particularly frustrating given the club’s ambitions after winning the Saudi Pro League title in 2025-26. The team currently sits third with 28 points from 12 matches, two points behind leaders Al-Hilal, although its rivals have a game in hand.



PositionClubMatchesW-D-LGoal DifferencePoints1.Al-Hilal1110-0-1+23302.Al-Qadsiah129-1-2+20283.Al-Nassr129-1-2+15284.Al-Ahli128-0-4+11245.Al-Ittihad117-3-1+1024Current Saudi Pro League standings



The club has still enjoyed an impressive campaign offensively, with Ronaldo scoring eight league goals and Joao Felix contributing seven assists. However, defensive vulnerabilities and a lack of midfield balance have become concerns, particularly following the departure of Marcelo Brozovic.



Recent defeat increases pressure on Ronaldo and Postecoglou



Al-Nassr’s 3-1 defeat to Al-Ahli on November 20 brought those weaknesses into sharper focus. Ronaldo opened the scoring but subsequently missed a penalty, allowing Al-Ahli to recover and eventually secure all three points.



Former Al-Nassr player Fuad Anwar criticized the Portuguese forward’s contribution, arguing that his missed spot-kick helped shift the momentum. “But he (Ronaldo) failed to convert the penalty that would have allowed Al-Nassr to stay in control, and that is what gave the Al-Ahli players the motivation to get back into the match, equalize and then win,” he told Arriyadiyah.









Anwar also defended Postecoglou, pointing to the club’s inability to strengthen during the summer transfer window. He believes the Australian coach has been left working with insufficient squad depth, particularly after Brozovic departed.



New source becomes main target of criticism



The wider frustration has now turned towards Al-Nassr’s ownership, with Saudi sports analyst Sultan Al-Otaibi delivering a particularly blunt assessment of the situation. In a post shared on social media, he argued that responsibility ultimately rests with those controlling the club’s major decisions.



“The primary and ultimate blame for Al Nassr’s problems lies solely with their owners. They’re the ones who appoint the officials, they’re the ones who approve the deals and contracts, and they’re the ones who reject them,” Al-Otaibi wrote on X (formerly Twitter).



Cristiano Ronaldo of Al Nassr celebrates with the Saudi Pro League Trophy.



His comments reflect growing criticism of the Public Investment Fund (PIF), which holds full ownership of Al-Nassr. Critics argue that the financial restrictions imposed by the fund have prevented the club from addressing important weaknesses, despite its continued ambitions to challenge for domestic and continental honors.



PIF’s involvement in financial supervision has also raised questions about the club’s executive structure. Reports of internal changes and restrictions on the authority of senior officials have added to concerns about stability and long-term planning.

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo and Lionel Messi share unwanted record as 21st-century penalty list revealed
items.description:
A new statistical comparison has highlighted an unusual side of their remarkable careers, placing the two superstars at the center of another unexpected discussion. 
Cristiano Ronaldo and Lionel Messi have spent nearly two decades competing for soccer’s biggest individual honors, setting extraordinary standards for goalscoring and consistency along the way. However, a new statistical comparison has highlighted an unusual side of their remarkable careers, placing the two superstars at the center of another unexpected discussion.



Both players have been trusted with penalty duties throughout their spells at some of the world’s biggest clubs and with their national teams. Their ability to deliver under pressure has produced countless memorable moments, although even the greatest forwards have occasionally struggled from 12 yards.



Ronaldo and Messi have taken considerably more penalties than most players of their generation, reflecting their longevity and importance to their respective teams. The Portuguese forward has generally maintained a higher conversion rate, while Messi’s numbers show that he has also been a regular presence at the spot throughout his career.



Career statistics through November 2026, excluding shootouts, show Ronaldo with 222 penalties taken and 184 scored, compared with Messi’s 150 attempts and 115 successful conversions. That gives Ronaldo an 82.9% conversion rate, while the Argentine stands at 76.7%.



Lionel Messi #10 of Inter Miami CF takes a penalty



Their records in penalty shootouts are similarly impressive. Ronaldo has scored 12 of his 14 attempts, while Messi has converted 11 of 13, demonstrating that both have regularly handled pressure when matches reach their decisive stages.



The players who have struggled most from 12 yards



The debate becomes particularly interesting when the focus shifts from successful penalties to missed opportunities. A ranking compiled using Transfermarkt data highlights several of the most prolific penalty takers in modern soccer, including some of the game’s most recognizable attacking stars.



Lionel Messi #10 of Inter Miami CF reacts after missing a penalty



The list features players from different generations and positions, ranging from established forwards to an unusually prolific penalty-taking defender. Brazil’s Hulk and Neymar are among the highest-ranked names, while former Barcelona, Real Madrid and Juventus stars also feature prominently.



Ronaldo and Messi lead the unwanted 21st-century ranking



According to the Transfermarkt figures, Ronaldo and Messi occupy the first two positions among players with the most penalties missed in the 21st century. Ronaldo tops the ranking after missing 40 penalties from 236 attempts, while Messi follows with 37 misses from 163 attempts. 



Cristiano Ronaldo of Al Nassr reacts after missing the penalty during



Despite having the highest number of unsuccessful spot-kicks, Ronaldo’s conversion rate remains approximately 83.1%, highlighting how frequently he has delivered throughout his career. The complete top 10 also includes several legendary forwards and attacking players:



RankPlayerPenalties takenMissed1.Cristiano Ronaldo236402.Lionel Messi163373.Hulk152274.James Tavernier103235.Neymar122226.Eran Zahavi95217.Dusan Tadic113218.Zlatan Ibrahimovic108199.Francesco Totti941910.Edinson Cavani9219



Hulk and Neymar are the closest challengers to the leading pair, with 27 and 22 missed penalties, respectively. Eran Zahavi and Dusan Tadic have each missed 21, while Ibrahimovic, Totti and Cavani complete the top 10 with 19 apiece.

items.title: Lionel Messi’s incident revives Cristiano Ronaldo’s 2024 controversy as Columbus Crew coach Laurent Courtois calls for red card
items.description:
Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo have both experienced moments when their on-field reactions sparked debate over how referees handle confrontations involving soccer's biggest stars. 
Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo have both experienced moments when their on-field reactions sparked debate over how referees handle confrontations involving soccer’s biggest stars. Messi’s latest controversy has brought fresh scrutiny to Inter Miami’s MLS Cup playoff campaign, with a rival coach questioning a major decision that could have consequences for the Argentine’s team.



The incident occurred during a difficult evening for the defending champions, who suffered a damaging defeat against Columbus Crew. While the result put Miami on the brink of elimination, the confrontation involving Messi quickly became one of the biggest talking points after the final whistle.



Miami entered its first-round meeting with Columbus on Saturday hoping to begin its title defence with a victory. Messi had received the MLS Golden Boot before kick-off, becoming the first player to win the award in consecutive seasons, but the celebrations soon gave way to frustration.



The Crew took the lead in the ninth minute after goalkeeper Dayne St. Clair brought down Gonzalo Tapia inside the penalty area. The Chilean forward converted the resulting spot-kick, while goalkeeper Patrick Schulte produced several important saves to keep Messi and Miami at bay.









The hosts’ situation deteriorated further in the 36th minute when Gonzalo Lujan received his second yellow card for a late challenge on Steven Moreira. Miami was left with 10 players for the remainder of the contest, giving Columbus a significant advantage.



Messi clashes with Tapia as tensions boil over



The most controversial moment arrived during first-half stoppage time, when Messi and Tapia became involved in an argument near the touchline. As the Argentine attempted to take a quick throw-in, the Columbus forward stood close to him and appeared to obstruct the restart.



Messi reacted by pushing the ball into Tapia’s face before throwing it towards his opponent’s head from close range. The Chilean went to ground, prompting protests from Columbus players and a heated exchange between members of both teams.



Lionel Messi takes a throw-in off Gonzalo Tapia’s face pic.twitter.com/jX3tTuojHe— Tom Bogert (@tombogert) November 22, 2026



Referee Allen Chapman showed both players a yellow card, allowing Messi to remain on the pitch. The decision immediately divided opinion, particularly because Miami was already trailing and playing with 10 men.



Columbus coach questions referee’s decision



Columbus head coach Laurent Courtois was particularly unhappy that Messi avoided a sending-off. The Crew manager believed the Argentine should have received a red card for his actions against Tapia. 



“Everybody knows that he deserved more than a yellow card,” Courtois said after the match. “It’s just really sad.” Chapman subsequently defended his decision when questioned by a pool reporter. “The force used was negligible, and the offense did not reach the level of violent conduct,” the referee explained.



Laurent Courtois sobre la tarjeta amarilla a Messi:“Todo el mundo sabe que eso era más que una amarilla”Además, le consulté si espera una revisión por parte de MLS.#InterMiamiCF #Crew96 pic.twitter.com/M4Oi3BeqwK— José Armando (@Jarm21) November 22, 2026



The distinction was central to the disciplinary debate, with Major League Soccer’s competition guidelines defining violent conduct as the use of excessive force or brutality when a player is not challenging for the ball. The Athletic refereeing expert Graham Scott reportedly argued that a red card would have been the more defensible decision, believing the contact was deliberate and excessive.



Why Messi’s incident recalls Ronaldo’s 2024 red card



The confrontation brought back memories of Cristiano Ronaldo’s straight red card against Al-Hilal in the Saudi Super Cup semi-final on April 8, 2024. The Al-Nassr forward became involved in a physical altercation with defender Saud Abdulhamid during a dispute over a throw-in, responding with aggressive physical contact that sent his opponent to the ground.



The referee dismissed the Portuguese for violent conduct, and Al-Nassr eventually lost 2-1. The incident resurfaced online alongside footage of Messi’s confrontation with Tapia, with fans debating whether the two superstars had been treated consistently. There were clear similarities in the circumstances, as the trigger was almost identical.



Many Ronaldo fans will swear this is not a Red card,That the system is always against him https://t.co/MBIcjQQ6bW pic.twitter.com/KPjg5RWa7p— Metua Metua (@Metuametua29) November 22, 2026



In both cases, an opponent stood close and actively impeded a quick throw-in, a common tactic to waste time or disrupt momentum. Players are required to retreat a reasonable distance, yet enforcement is often inconsistent. What’s more, both Messi and Ronaldo, known more for brilliance than volatility, lost composure in the heat of a competitive fixture when their team was struggling. 



These are not random acts of aggression but responses to perceived gamesmanship. The opponent went down in each case, leading to questions of whether the contact was violent enough for a red card. The Argentine used the ball; the Portuguese used his body.



Lionel Messi drilled Gonzalo Tapia in the head with this throw-in pic.twitter.com/TEwPTFvMSK— Jomboy Media (@JomboyMedia) November 22, 2026



While the situations rhyme, they are not identical. Messi directed a ball at an opponent’s face from very short range; Ronaldo made direct physical contact with his body. Laws of the Game treat excessive force or violent conduct more severely when it involves striking or headbutting than when the object is a ball, though intent and force still matter.

items.title: Madness erupts as Sevilla deny Betis in wild end to Spain’s ‘derby of derbies’
items.description: Rivals have been heading in opposite directions in recent years but latest clash showed some things never change“If we didn’t celebrate a goal, especially in this game, that would be madness,” Kike Salas said. Instead, this was madness, the kind of moment a derby is meant to have, even if it has nothing else. It was late, it was lucky, and there wasn’t even a winner but right there, right then, at 24 minutes past 8pm on Saturday evening in the Ramón Sánchez-Pizjuán Stadium, it felt like there was. Frankly it was a bit rubbish, as bad a goal as you’ll see, but it was also the best, practically Pelé against the Nazis. Suddenly there were arms and legs everywhere, tears too. Cameras confirmed it. Zoom in and there they are: actual, real life tears.In the 91st minute of the 146th meeting between Sevilla Fútbol Club and Real Betis Balompié – “derby of derbies” according to Luis García, the Sevilla coach for whom it was the first – Salas’s shot from 18 yards went through Marc Bartra’s legs and Álvaro Valles’s hands. The ball dribbled into the Betis net so apologetically it barely touched the net at all and hadn’t got there before Sevilla’s vice-captain was gone. Raised in Morón de la Frontera, to the south of a city divided, Salas joined Sevilla at 11; now, having levelled the game at 1-1, he went tearing towards the terraces, absolutely losing it like they were. items.title: Mauricio Pochettino can now see just how desperate Manchester United are | Jonathan Wilson
items.description: The manager’s first game in charge was a disaster and he needs to lift the mood within a sunken squad if a relegation battle is to be avoidedSign up for our free newsletter hereIn as much as any derby can ever be a free hit, there was always a sense that Mauricio Pochettino’s first game as Manchester United manager wouldn’t matter too much; nobody expected them to win away to Liverpool. This was not a game on which anybody was going to judge him, and that feeling only magnified when Leny Yoro was sent off after eight minutes. United’s victory at Anfield last season was their first for a decade; what’s difficult to do with 11 men is only going to get harder playing a man down for 82 minutes. But that does not mean that it did not matter.Although Roy Keane was determined to reject the suggestion, there was perhaps even some credit to be gleaned from having lost only 4-0. Certainly when they were 2-0 down after 13 minutes, there was reason for United to fear an embarrassment akin to their 7-0 defeat against Liverpool in 2023. Perhaps Pochettino deserves credit for his switch to a back three, which brought a degree of stabilisation, but United could easily have lost far more comfortably than they did. Liverpool had 18 shots in the game three-and-a-half years ago, eight of them on target; on Sunday they had 28, 11 of them on target. When you’ve conceded an xG of 4.38, there’s not much point quibbling over the details; you’ve been hammered. Continue reading...

items.title: Lionel Messi’s USA era draws fresh attention after Son Heung-Min agrees with Thomas Muller as MLS comes under fire over one major problem
items.description:
As the league continues to grow and welcome established international names, questions remain over whether its competitive structure provides the intensity players are accustomed to in Europe. 
Lionel Messi‘s arrival in the United States has helped Major League Soccer attract unprecedented attention, with fellow stars Son Heung-Min and Thomas Muller also bringing considerable experience from European soccer. However, as the league continues to grow and welcome established international names, questions remain over whether its competitive structure provides the intensity players are accustomed to in Europe.



Son has now added his voice to a debate started by Muller, agreeing with the Vancouver Whitecaps forward’s assessment of the differences between MLS and Europe’s leading competitions. Both players have experienced soccer at the highest level, making their comments particularly significant as the American league looks to strengthen its global reputation.



Muller, who joined the Vancouver Whitecaps in 2025 after a distinguished career with Bayern Munich, recently discussed the challenges of comparing MLS with European leagues. The German World Cup winner suggested that the American competition operates under a different level of pressure because of its unique structure. Speaking to Global News, the German explained: “It’s difficult to compare because of the system. There is no relegation, there is no big pressure.



“There is, ‘Oh yeah, we do a rebuild.’ Nobody’s happy to lose, but it’s totally different when you fight [against] getting relegated.” He also highlighted the consequences European clubs face when they drop into a lower division, including reduced budgets, potential job losses and uncertainty over players’ contracts. Those stakes, he argued, can dramatically change how teams approach matches, particularly when they face opponents fighting to avoid relegation.



Thomas Müller was not offering criticism just a comparison of systems & the competitive reality in Major League Soccer."There is no big pressure. When you play a bottom of the table team in Europe, they fight for their life." Listen 👇Courtesy of Global News#ProRelForUSA… pic.twitter.com/xFWM0l1NDn— Glenn Crooks (@GlennCrooks) November 19, 2026 



Muller added that MLS teams can sometimes appear more relaxed defensively, describing the approach as “laissez faire”. While he acknowledged that this can produce entertaining attacking soccer, he suggested it can also affect the consistency and intensity of performances across 90 minutes.



Son Heung-Min gives his verdict



The former Tottenham forward was subsequently asked about Muller’s assessment and whether he had experienced similar differences during his time in MLS. Son, who joined LAFC, made his position clear by agreeing with the German’s observations.



“I think Thomas Muller was spot on,” the 34-year-old forward said. “MLS is growing significantly, and big-name players are coming into the league. But sometimes you do feel there’s less pressure because there’s no relegation. You can finish near the bottom and still remain in the league.”



🚨 𝐒𝐎𝐍 𝐇𝐄𝐔𝐍𝐆-𝐌𝐈𝐍: "𝐓𝐇𝐎𝐌𝐀𝐒 𝐌Ü𝐋𝐋𝐄𝐑 𝐖𝐀𝐒 𝐒𝐏𝐎𝐓 𝐎𝐍, 𝐒𝐎𝐌𝐄𝐓𝐈𝐌𝐄𝐒 𝐘𝐎𝐔 𝐅𝐄𝐄𝐋 𝐓𝐇𝐄𝐑𝐄'𝐒 𝐋𝐄𝐒𝐒 𝐏𝐑𝐄𝐒𝐒𝐔𝐑𝐄 𝐈𝐍 𝐌𝐋𝐒 𝐁𝐄𝐂𝐀𝐔𝐒𝐄 𝐓𝐇𝐄𝐑𝐄'𝐒 𝐍𝐎 𝐑𝐄𝐋𝐄𝐆𝐀𝐓𝐈𝐎𝐍"❓ "Yesterday, Thomas Müller said there wasn't much…— The Nassr Tribune™️ (@AlNassrTribune) November 22, 2026 



The South Korean international stressed that he enjoys playing in the United States and remains focused on representing LAFC and his country. However, he believes the contrast with European soccer is difficult to ignore.



The absence of relegation at the heart of the debate



Son’s agreement with Muller brings the central issue into focus: MLS does not have a promotion and relegation system, meaning clubs cannot be demoted after finishing at the bottom of the standings. Unlike in the Premier League or Bundesliga, teams struggling throughout the campaign do not face the threat of losing their place in the top division.



The South Korean international drew on his experience in England, where he spent years playing for Tottenham, to explain why the pressure can feel different. “I also played in the Premier League, where you face enormous pressure every single week, sometimes every three days,” he said.



Son Heung-Min of Los Angeles FC



“If you’re not performing, if you’re not playing well, or if your team starts struggling and finds itself near the bottom of the table, you go through a difficult period.” Son believes those survival battles make competition more exciting for both players and supporters.



He also encouraged MLS officials to examine the issue, adding: “I think that makes the competition more fun. I want the best for MLS, and I hope they look into this and perhaps consider making some changes.”



Why MLS is unlikely to introduce relegation



The current system is closely connected to the financial structure of American professional sports. MLS operates through franchises, with owners investing in clubs that benefit from the security of guaranteed participation in the top division.



Introducing relegation could put those investments at risk, potentially reducing franchise values and making the league less attractive to prospective owners. The change would also require significant restructuring and approval from the investors who control the clubs.



Incoming MLS commissioner Larry Berg previously ruled out the prospect of introducing relegation, arguing that it would not help secure investment in stadiums, training facilities and playing squads. His comments underline how difficult it would be for the league to move away from its established model.



Lionel Messi #10 of Inter Miami CF is presented with the 2025 Landon Donovan MLS MVP trophy



Messi’s MLS experience adds another dimension



The debate also raises questions about the balance between competitive pressure and the league’s efforts to create parity. Eighteen of MLS’s 30 teams qualify for the playoffs, giving a large proportion of the competition a chance to win the title even after an inconsistent regular season.



Inter Miami provided a notable example in 2024, when Messi’s team finished with the league’s best regular-season record but was eliminated by Atlanta United in the opening round. Atlanta had finished 34 points behind Miami, demonstrating how the playoff format can produce unexpected outcomes.



Lionel Messi #10 of Inter Miami CF lifts the Champion’s trophy after winning the Audi 2025 MLS Cup Final



MLS also uses mechanisms such as designated player restrictions and the draft to maintain a degree of balance between teams. While those rules can help prevent financial dominance by a small number of clubs, critics argue that the system does not impose enough consequences on underperforming sides.



Neither Son nor Muller has suggested that MLS lacks quality or ambition. Their comments instead highlight a structural difference that could become increasingly important as the league attracts more players with experience of Europe’s most demanding competitions.

items.title: Lamine Yamal breaks La Liga record for all the wrong reasons as Kylian Mbappe comparison haunts Barcelona star
items.description:
The teenager still played a decisive role in the comeback, but his latest setback has drawn attention to an issue that could become increasingly significant as comparisons with Kylian Mbappe continue. 
Lamine Yamal endured a frustrating moment during Barcelona’s dramatic victory over Villarreal, adding another unwanted talking point to an otherwise impressive performance. The teenager still played a decisive role in the comeback, but his latest setback has drawn attention to an issue that could become increasingly significant as comparisons with Kylian Mbappe continue.



Barcelona produced an impressive second-half comeback to defeat Villarreal 3-2 at Spotify Camp Nou on Sunday, despite falling two goals behind inside the opening seven minutes. Tajon Buchanan opened the scoring in the fifth minute before Tani Oluwaseyi doubled the visitors’ advantage just 128 seconds later.



Hansi Flick’s side struggled early on, with a makeshift defence featuring Frenkie de Jong at centre-back because of injuries to Andreas Christensen and Pau Cubarsi. Villarreal took full advantage, leaving the La Liga champions facing an uphill battle in front of their home supporters.



The Blaugrana eventually found their rhythm after the break, with Gerard Martin reducing the deficit in the 57th minute. Fermin Lopez then levelled the score following excellent work from Yamal, before Pau Navarro turned an Eric Garcia cross into his own net to complete the turnaround.









However, one first-half moment drew particular attention. After winning a penalty, Yamal stepped up to take responsibility but sent his effort against the right-hand post, missing an opportunity to bring Barcelona back into the contest earlier.



Yamal enters La Liga history for the wrong reason



The missed spot-kick carried a significant statistical consequence. According to figures highlighted by Spanish statistician Alexis, known as MisterChip, Yamal has now missed three of the seven penalties he has taken in La Liga, with two of those attempts striking the post.



At 19 years and 132 days old, he has become the youngest player in La Liga history to miss three penalties. He surpassed Fernando Torres, who reached the same unwanted milestone at 20 years and 64 days in 2004.



RankPlayerAge when missing third penaltyYear1.Lamine Yamal19 years, 132 days20262.Fernando Torres20 years, 64 days20043.López Ufarte20 years, 312 days19794.Lafuente21 years, 174 days1929Youngest players to miss three penalties in La Liga history



The historical list also includes Lopez Ufarte, who was 20 years and 312 days old when he missed his third penalty in 1979, and Lafuente, who reached the mark at 21 years and 174 days in 1929. Yamal’s record is particularly striking given how early in his senior career he has already taken responsibility from the spot.



Lamine Yamal of FC Barcelona looks on



Mbappe comparison adds another layer to the debate



Yamal’s penalty struggles have also invited comparisons with Real Madrid forward Kylian Mbappe, who has faced criticism over his own record from 12 yards. The Frenchman recently missed a penalty against Celta Vigo, failing to convert an opportunity that could have helped his team equalize.



RankPlayerPenalties missedAttemptsMiss rate1.Kylian Mbappe52321.7%2.Vedat Muriqi31030.0%2.Robert Lewandowski3742.9%Most La Liga penalties missed since the start of 2024–25



MisterChip also suggests that Mbappe has missed five of his 23 La Liga penalties since the beginning of the 2024-25 season, more than any other player in the competition over that period. Vedat Muriqi and Robert Lewandowski follow with three misses each.



PlayerPenalties missedAttemptsMiss rateKylian Mbappe52321.7%Lamine Yamal3742.9%Mbappe vs. Yamal: Penalty miss rates



The difference becomes more noticeable when looking at their respective conversion rates. Yamal has missed three of seven attempts, while the Frenchman has missed five of 23, giving the Barcelona teenager a considerably higher failure rate.

items.title: Getafe vs Atletico Madrid: Confirmed lineups for the 2026-27 LaLiga match
items.description:
Take a look at the projected lineups for Getafe vs Atletico Madrid in the 2026-27 LaLiga. Getafe host Atletico Madrid in a LaLiga meeting between a side fighting to stop the bleeding at home and a visitor still chasing consistency on the road.
Getafe have dropped two of their last three, falling 0-2 to Villarreal on November 8 and 0-4 to Athletic on October 25, sandwiched around a 3-1 win over Sevilla on November 1. The heavy loss to Athletic exposed problems defensively, and the Villarreal result did nothing to settle those nerves. A home game against Atletico Madrid now carries real weight for Getafe as they try to steady themselves before the fixtures pile up.
Atletico Madrid also enter on a mixed run, losing 1-2 to Barcelona on November 8 after back-to-back wins over Levante on October 31 and Deportivo on October 24. Those two victories came by matching 2-0 and 1-0 scorelines, suggesting a team that can grind out results even without scoring freely. A win at Getafe would help Atletico Madrid answer questions raised by the Barcelona defeat and keep pace in the table.
Getafe confirmed lineup
Jose Bordalas sets Getafe up in a 3-4-1-2, with Dávid Soria in goal behind a back three of Sebastián Boselli, Zaid Romero and Andrés García. Dani Carvajal and Djené provide width as wing-backs, with Ramón Terrats and Orel Mangala holding the midfield and Johan Mojica pushing on from the back line. Martín Satriano and Enes Ünal lead the attack, with the pairing suggesting Bordalás wants a direct, physical approach against Atletico’s back line. Getafe are without Juanmi Jiménez, Chrisantus Uche and Nemanja Gudelj, all out, which thins their attacking and midfield options and puts more responsibility on Satriano and Ünal up front.
Getafe confirmed starting XI (4-4-2): Dávid Soria, Dani Carvajal, Jean Ives Valou, Djené, Johan Mojica, Andrés García, Mario Martín, Orel Mangala, Ramón Terrats, Enes Ünal, Martín Satriano. Coach: José Bordalás.
Atletico Madrid confirmed lineup
Diego Simeone lines Atletico Madrid up in a 4-3-3, with Jan Oblak behind a back four of Marcos Llorente, Robin Le Normand, Dávid Hancko and Alex Grimaldo. Pablo Barrios, Koke and Johnny Cardoso make up a midfield built for control, while Giuliano Simeone, Julián Alvarez and Álex Baena offer pace and movement across the front line. That trio gives Atletico Madrid options to stretch Getafe’s back three and exploit space behind the wing-backs. Alejandro Grimaldo and Cristian Romero are both out, a notable loss on the defensive side that could test the depth of Atletico Madrid’s back line against a Getafe team set up to press and disrupt.
Atletico Madrid confirmed starting XI (4-3-3): Jan Oblak, Marcos Llorente, Robin Le Normand, Dávid Hancko, Alex Grimaldo, Johnny Cardoso, Koke, Pablo Barrios, Giuliano Simeone, Julián Alvarez, Álex Baena. Coach: Diego Simeone.

items.description:
Take a look at the projected lineups for AC Milan vs Frosinone in the 2026-27 Serie A. Milan host Frosinone at San Siro with both sides fresh off contrasting midweek results, and this one carries real weight for the home side’s push up the table.
AC Milan arrive on the back of a 2-1 win over Genoa on November 8, which followed a 3-1 statement win over Inter on October 31. Those two results papered over a 2-4 loss to Bologna on October 28, and the Genoa win suggests the defending issues from that Bologna game have been addressed. A third straight win would keep Milan firmly in touch with the top of the table.
Frosinone come in off a 0-1 loss to Cagliari on November 7, a result that snapped the momentum built by a 2-0 win over Torino on November 1 and a 5-1 rout of Lecce on October 29. The Cagliari defeat was their first in three outings, and a positive result at San Siro would steady things after that setback. Points on the road against a team like Milan would be a strong marker for where Frosinone stand this season.
AC Milan confirmed lineup
Amorim sets Milan up in a 4-4-1-1 with Mike Maignan behind a back four of Mario Gila, Koni De Winter, Strahinja Pavlović and Sankhoun Diawara. Yunus Musah and Adrien Rabiot anchor the midfield, with Christian Pulisic and Diego Moreira providing width to support Luka Modrić just behind Gonçalo Ramos up top. There are no listed absences, so Amorim has his preferred group available, and the shape allows Modrić freedom to drift into pockets while Ramos leads the line alone.
AC Milan confirmed starting XI (4-4-1-1): Mike Maignan, Mario Gila, Koni De Winter, Sankhoun Diawara, Davide Bartesaghi, Yunus Musah, Adrien Rabiot, Christian Pulisic, Luka Modrić, Diego Moreira, Gonçalo Ramos. Coach: Ruben Amorim.
Frosinone confirmed lineup
Alvini goes with a 4-2-3-1 for Frosinone, with Lorenzo Palmisani in goal behind Anthony Oyono, Gabriele Calvani, Ilario Monterisi and Enzo Tchato. Patrizio Masini and Giacomo Calò sit as the double pivot, screening for an attacking trio of Romano Schmid, Farès Ghedjemis and Giorgi Kvernadze behind lone striker Daniel Bîrligea. With no absences reported, Alvini can field his full-strength setup, leaning on Kvernadze and Ghedjemis to combine around Bîrligea on the counter.
Frosinone confirmed starting XI (4-2-3-1): Lorenzo Palmisani, Anthony Oyono, Gabriele Calvani, Ilario Monterisi, Enzo Tchato, Patrizio Masini, Romano Schmid, Giorgio Cittadini, Farès Ghedjemis, Giorgi Kvernadze, Giacomo Calò. Coach: Massimiliano Alvini.

items.title: Liverpool vs Manchester United: Confirmed lineups for the 2026-27 Premier League match
items.description:
Take a look at the projected lineups for Liverpool vs Manchester United in the 2026-27 Premier League. Anfield hosts another chapter of the oldest rivalry in English football, with Liverpool and Manchester United both looking to settle some nerves after uneven stretches through November.
Liverpool arrive off a 3-1 win over Crystal Palace on November 8, a result that followed a 0-1 loss to Arsenal and a 2-0 win over Albion in late October. The mix of results shows a team capable of bouncing back quickly after a setback. Three points here would put them back on more stable footing in the table.
Manchester United come in off a wild 4-4 draw with Aston Villa on November 8, sandwiched between a 0-2 loss to Chelsea on October 31 and a 0-3 defeat to Bournemouth on October 25. That stretch has produced just one point from three matches and no clean sheet in any of them. A result at Anfield would go a long way toward steadying a side short on momentum.
Liverpool confirmed lineup
Andoni Iraola projects a 4-2-3-1 built around pace and movement in behind, with Alexander Isak leading the line and support from Florian Wirtz and Cody Gakpo in the attacking midfield band. Dominik Szoboszlai and Alexis Mac Allister anchor the double pivot, giving the side control through the middle, while Ronald Araujo and Jérémy Jacquet flank Virgil van Dijk in defense. The absences of Ryan Gravenberch, Jeremie Frimpong, Conor Bradley, Giovanni Leoni, Amara Nallo and Hugo Ekitiké strip out depth across midfield, both fullback spots and the forward line, leaving Iraola with a leaner squad to rotate from if changes are needed.
Liverpool confirmed starting XI (4-2-3-1): Alisson, Ronald Araujo, Jérémy Jacquet, Virgil Van Dijk, Miloš Kerkez, Dominik Szoboszlai, Florian Wirtz, Alexis Mac Allister, Rio Ngumoha, Alexander Isak, Bradley Barcola. Coach: Andoni Iraola.
Manchester United confirmed lineup
Mauricio Pochettino also sets up in a 4-2-3-1, with Bruno Fernandes and Amad Diallo pushed forward off Matheus Cunha and Bryan Mbeumo providing the attacking threat. Youri Tielemans and Kobbie Mainoo sit in front of a back four of Dalot, Martínez, Maguire and Yoro, a pairing tasked with controlling tempo against a Liverpool midfield that includes Wirtz and Mac Allister. United are without Marcus Rashford, Benjamin Šeško and Manuel Ugarte up front and through midfield, and Luke Shaw’s absence at left back adds to the defensive questions Pochettino has to manage heading into this one.
Manchester United confirmed starting XI (4-2-3-1): Senne Lammens, Leny Yoro, Matthijs De Ligt, Lisandro Martínez, Diogo Dalot, Youri Tielemans, Bruno Fernandes, Kobbie Mainoo, Patrick Dorgu, Bryan Mbeumo, Matheus Cunha. Coach: Mauricio Pochettino.

items.title: Danny Kelly loved football and never forgot the absurdity of earning a living talking about it | Max Rushden
items.description: The journalist and broadcaster who died last week aged 69 knew the enduring power of radio, even as the landscape changed so quicklyIt’s injury time at the Emirates on 29 October 2008, Arsenal are 4-3 up against Tottenham. Tom Huddlestone cushions a ball to Luka Modric, whose strike takes a deflection. It loops over Manuel Almunia and off a post into the path of Aaron Lennon, who prods it home and starts skipping towards the Spurs supporters before diving on to the ground and being enveloped by Modric, Benoît Assou-Ekotto, Darren Bent and a couple of pitch-invading fans. Pandemonium, for once, seems the apt way to describe it.But the real entertainment is happening in a radio studio at 18 Hatfields, London SE1; the old home of TalkSport. As the goal goes in, a guttural voice makes an indecipherable but very loud noise. It’s hard to transcribe – perhaps “ERRRRRAAAARRRGGHH”, or maybe “OOEEERRAAGGH”. It’s just a noise, but it’s unmistakably Danny Kelly. He regains the power of speech and follows it up with: “Gooooaaaal … Goalll Stan, Goalll at the Emirates.” Reporter Ian Abrahams and Stan Collymore join the excitement, before Danny comes back: “I LOVE FOOTBALL, STAN, I LOVE IT.” It is such a brilliant piece of radio. From one of the absolute greats. Continue reading...

items.title: WSL talking points: Chelsea’s gamble pays off and have Arsenal lost fear factor?
items.description: Blues beat champions after bold substitution and Gunners’ home struggles continue with fifth consecutive WSL drawSonia Bompastor attempted to deflect suggestions that the removal of Kadeisha Buchanan 12 minutes into Chelsea’s top-of-the-table clash with Manchester City was tactical, but few were convinced by the claim that it was down to injury. The manager said the centre-back, who had not asked to come off and walked straight down the tunnel, had taken a knock to the head in training and been assessed and cleared, but that during the game “she was not herself”. On came Veerle Buurman and the threat of Khadija Shaw was nullified, the Dutch defender restricting the golden boot favourite so well that Shaw did not manage a shot on target. Bompastor said after the game that she had not spoken to Buchanan but that she would “explain myself to her”. “I always have good relationships with the players, bring them clarity, and I’m always direct and honest so they have the information,” she said. “It won’t be any different.” Enforced or not, the substitution was a huge gamble that paid off, even after the loss of Melvine Malard to injury in the first half reduced their number of remaining in-game substitution windows to one. Suzanne WrackMatch report: Chelsea 1-0 Manchester City Continue reading...

items.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future successRead the full updates on our class of 2021 here and hereIn 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series.We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well).The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players.The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. items.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individualsWhat makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature. My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career.After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
